text:
ConocoPhillips fell 2.3% today after oil prices dropped sharply on renewed diplomatic efforts to end the Iran-Israel conflict. On October 27th, news that Iran's supreme leader and top security official were discussing ceasefire conditions sent crude lower—US oil fell from recent highs, and the stock followed. The company had surged 5% over the past two weeks on Middle East tensions driving crude to six-month highs around $116/barrel, so today's retreat reversed some of those recent gains as geopolitical risk eased.

The core issue for oil stocks like this one is that their profits move directly with crude prices. When tensions spike, oil rises and refiners benefit; when diplomatic progress suggests those tensions might ease, prices fall and so do the stocks. The last few days show this clearly—the stock jumped to $150.80 on October 23rd as crude hit $116, then fell back today as peace talks overshadowed the supply-risk narrative.
